label: copy phase: fed-back input h (just output an h), later in the copy
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and only when the input is the letter h, i.e. the model just output h (orig(recall_idx-1) == h). In the copy phase it fires on about 58% of h inputs overall, and on nearly all of them from recall_idx 4 onward. It is weak or silent for h inputs early in the copy (recall_idx 1-2), and the activation rises with recall_idx/t (rate about 0.8% at recall 2, about 3% from recall 4 on; the largest activations come at mid-to-late copy positions). It never fires in the original phase or at <DEL>, and never on any token other than h (a handful of p/u cases aside). When h appears twice in a row in the copy, the second h activates less strongly. It does not depend on which token is output next or on the first token.

issues: The explanation gets the early-copy rates wrong. It says the rate at recall_idx 2 is about 0.8%, but that is the rate over all steps at recall_idx 2. Among copy-phase h inputs at recall_idx 2 the feature is active 24% of the time (precision 0.236, n=16724). Calling it 'weak or silent' at recall_idx 1-2 is only right for recall_idx 1, where it fires 23 times in about 16.7k h inputs.

Activation on copy-phase h inputs rises gradually with recall_idx; there is no clean cutoff. Precision is 0.24 at recall_idx 2, 0.64 at 3, 0.89 at 4 and 0.93 at 5 and above. At recall_idx 3 the feature is active on about two thirds of h inputs, not silent. The recall_idx>=3 cutoff is a reasonable threshold on this gradient, which is why the remaining false positives are concentrated at recall_idx 3-4: about 5.8k at 3, 1.6k at 4 and 1.9k at 5 and above on dev.

The other claims check out. All active steps are in the copy phase (none in the original phase or at <DEL>). 52713 of 52757 active steps have h as input, with 43 p and 1 u. After a preceding copy-phase h, precision drops to 0.66, and the top examples show the second h weaker. first_tok and next_out have flat profiles.

No systematic false-positive or missed class was found on the test misses beyond the recall_idx gradient. False-positive precision barely moves when conditioned on a digit or vowel as previous token, digits seen, in_count, to_go==0 or next_out being a digit (0.81-0.87). L has only a mild effect (precision 0.73 for L<=5 vs 0.85 for L>=8). Splitting recall_idx 2-3 by L did not separate active from inactive cases. Misses are mostly weak recall_idx 2 h activations, which hold 2.8% of the activation mass.
Test scores reproduce: precision 0.839, recall 0.925, F1 0.880, mass recall 0.972.
